\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Noise --- Duality: Results}

\begin{lemma}[An $L^q$ bound from bounded pairings]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.eLpNorm_le_of_bounded_pairing}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.eLpNorm_le_of_bounded_pairing}
\leanok
\difficulty{6}
Let $(\alpha,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $q>1$, and let $u:\alpha\to\mathbb R$ be
integrable. Suppose $C\ge0$ and, for every essentially bounded measurable
$g:\alpha\to\mathbb R$, the absolute value of $\int u g\,d\mu$ is at most $C$ times the
$L^{q/(q-1)}(\mu)$ norm of $g$. Let $v:\alpha\to\mathbb R$ be almost everywhere strongly
measurable, nonnegative almost everywhere, and satisfy $v\le |u|$ almost everywhere;
suppose also that $v\le B$ almost everywhere for some real number $B$. Then the
$L^q(\mu)$ norm of $v$ is at most $C$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Integrability from bounded pairings]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.memLp_and_eLpNorm_le_of_bounded_pairing}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.memLp_and_eLpNorm_le_of_bounded_pairing}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.eLpNorm_le_of_bounded_pairing}
\difficulty{4}
Let $(\alpha,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $q>1$, and let $u:\alpha\to\mathbb R$ be
integrable. Suppose $C\ge0$ and, for every essentially bounded measurable
$g:\alpha\to\mathbb R$,
\[\left|\int u g\,d\mu\right|\le C\,\|g\|_{q/(q-1)},\]
where the norm is the extended $L^{q/(q-1)}$ norm converted to a real number. Then $u$
belongs to $L^q(\mu)$ and its extended $L^q$ norm is at most $C$.
\end{lemma}
